- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 72.5), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above prior high or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3 consecutive negative sentiment values), model underreacts to downward trend; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast.
- Model frequently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 73.0 and sentiment is neutral or positive, reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with recent 10-day average.
- When sentiment turns negative after a positive spike, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply 2–4% downward correction within first 3 days of negative sentiment onset.
